title: [Feature Request] Implement Alibaba CEDAR Two-Stage Residual Decomposition & Cross-Attention Alignment (arXiv:2608.25871v1)
body:
## 📌 Feature Description
Implement Alibaba 1688's Two-Stage Decoupled Residual Decomposition architecture from Meng et al. (arXiv:2608.25871v1): *CEDAR: Controlled and Event-Driven Demand Forecasting via Residual Decomposition*.

### 🧮 Two-Stage System Formulation
- Formally decouples quantitative baseline state transitions from qualitative event shock perturbations:
  $$\mathbf{s}_{t+1} = f_\theta(\mathbf{s}_{\leq t}, \mathbf{a}_{\leq t+1}) + \epsilon_t$$
- Stage 1: Noise Filtering & Energy Tag Extraction (discards non-commercial entertainment/gossip noise).
- Stage 2: Regional Synthesis with Scheduled Calendar Events to estimate residual shock perturbation $\epsilon_t$.

title: [Feature Request] Ingest Zero-Cost Energy Data Feeds (FRED, EIA v2, Universal State Open Data, USDA Biofuels, Open-Meteo)
body:
## Summary
Supersedes closed issue #134 (which proposed the paid Apify `crawlerbros/fuel-prices-scraper`). In accordance with project policy barring paid Apify tools due to subscription and compute unit costs, this issue tracks the ingestion of 5 zero-cost, open-access fuel and energy data sources to validate and improve model forecasting accuracy:

1. **FRED (St. Louis Fed) API**: Weekly national & PADD retail gasoline/diesel series (`GASREGW`, `GASDESW`, `GASREGWCW`, `GASREGWGULF`) and CPI gasoline index (`CUUR0000SETB01`).
2. **U.S. EIA API v2 (`api.eia.gov`)**: Direct weekly retail price series, refinery percent utilization, and PADD-level fuel/crude stock inventories (`/petroleum/pri/gnd/data/`, `/petroleum/pnp/pct/data/`, `/petroleum/stoc/wstk/data/`).
3. **Universal State Open Data Portals Connector (`src/state_open_data.py`)**: A generalized zero-cost open data client querying Socrata (`data.<state>.gov` / `data.gov`), CKAN, and state revenue APIs for fuel tax rates, excise updates, and motor fuel sales volumes across **all 50 US States** (extending beyond initial target states).
4. **USDA Biofuel & Ethanol Market Reports (`marsapi.ams.usda.gov`)**: Spot Midwest ethanol rack prices ($/gal) and RIN D6 Ethanol Credit spot values for E10 unleaded blendstock cost modeling.
5. **Open-Meteo & NOAA High-Resolution Degree Days (`api.open-meteo.com`)**: High-resolution Heating Degree Days (HDD), Cooling Degree Days (CDD), and regional temperature shocks across major refining hubs.

title: [Feature Request] Evaluate Microsoft Qlib & RD-Agent Architecture for Automated Alpha Factor Discovery & Dynamic Domain Adaptation

### Summary
Evaluate and ingest architectural patterns from Microsoft Research's **Qlib** quantitative platform ([microsoft/qlib](https://github.com/microsoft/qlib)) and **RD-Agent** ([microsoft/RD-Agent](https://github.com/microsoft/RD-Agent)) into the midgley quantitative fuel price prediction framework.

### Background & Rationale
Microsoft Qlib provides state-of-the-art quantitative infrastructure for financial and commodity time-series forecasting. Combining Qlib with RD-Agent enables **automated factor discovery**, **factor-model co-optimization**, and **dynamic domain adaptation (DDG-DA)** to handle non-stationary market distributions (regime shifts). Empirical benchmarks show RD-Agent(Q) achieving ~2x higher annualized returns with ~70% fewer factors compared to static rule sets.

### Key Objectives & Proposed Implementation

1. **Automated LLM Factor Mining (RD-Agent Pattern):**
   - Implement an autonomous factor discovery sub-agent loop using Gemini 2.5 Flash.
   - Formulate financial hypotheses on non-linear interactions across alternative data streams (Cboe OVX volatility, Baker Hughes rig counts, NOAA convective weather risk scores, Cushing WTI spreads, and regional rack margins).
   - Automatically write, test, evaluate, and prune candidate factor expressions in Python.

2. **Market Dynamics & Concept Drift Adaptation (DDG-DA):**
   - Evaluate Qlib's Dynamic Data Grouping Domain Adaptation framework to dynamically re-weight base estimators (Ridge / XGBoost) during structural market breaks (e.g., OPEC emergency production shifts, major pipeline blockades, or policy updates).

3. **Symbolic Domain Expressions & Point-in-Time Integrity:**
   - Benchmark Qlib-style rolling symbolic expressions (e.g., $close / Ref(, 1) - 1, rolling z-scores) for lightweight, high-performance feature calculations.
   - Integrate point-in-time calculation constraints to eliminate look-ahead leakage during multi-horizon out-of-time backtesting.

### Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Research prototype demonstrating LLM factor discovery with automatic factor scoring and backtest validation.
- [ ] Benchmark comparing dynamic domain adaptation vs baseline Ridge/XGBoost regular models.
- [ ] Integration documentation added to docs/ and AGENTS.md.

title: [Feature Request] Implement Bitemporal Vintage Tracking (as_of) for EIA Data Ingestion
body:
## Context & Motivation
Government energy sources like the US Energy Information Administration (EIA) routinely issue inline revisions and historical restatements (e.g., weekly crude stock levels, motor gasoline demand, refinery runs) weeks after first publication.

Inspired by the bitemporal data architecture pattern in [oldhero5/energex](https://github.com/oldhero5/energex), storing only valid period timestamps without tracking release dates (\^Gs_of\ / knowledge time) introduces subtle lookahead bias when backtesting or retraining quantitative models on historical EIA figures.

## Proposed Solution
1. Extend \src/alternative_data_feeds.py\ and EIA ingestion routines to attach an explicit \^Gs_of\ publication timestamp or vintage metadata tag to ingested EIA observation records.
2. Implement an honesty flag (\intage_reconstructed=True\) when backfilling historical baselines vs live-logged observations.
3. Ensure quantitative estimators (\src/models.py\) and feature engineering routines (\src/feature_engineering.py\) filter features by \^Gs_of <= target_run_date\ during historical backtests.

## Benefits
- Prevents lookahead leakage in quantitative model backtesting and retrains.
- Ensures 100% point-in-time correct data integrity for EIA fundamental series.

title: [Feature Request] Implement System Telemetry & Observability Metrics Engine for Grafana (Token Usage, API Quotas, Latency & Errors)
body:
## Terminology Note
The industry standard terms for tracking non-mathematical compute performance, token consumption, API limits, runtime latencies, and system errors are:
- **System Telemetry / Operational Telemetry**
- **Observability**
- **Operational Metrics (Compute/System Metrics)**
- **Application Performance Monitoring (APM)**

This issue proposes introducing a central telemetry collector to feed real-time compute performance metrics into Grafana dashboards.

---

## Summary
Implement a central **Telemetry & Observability Engine** (`src/telemetry.py` or `/metrics` exporter) across the multi-agent pipeline to track operational compute performance, LLM token consumption, API quota burn rates, execution runtime latencies, and system exceptions—with built-in support for **Multi-Environment Telemetry (`dev` vs `prod`)**.

---

## Multi-Environment Tracking (`dev` vs `prod`)

To allow tracking dev work on feature/dev branches separately from live production executions in Grafana dashboards:
- **Global Metric Labels:** Every emitted metric will automatically include an `environment` label (`environment="dev"` or `environment="prod"`), determined dynamically via the `MIDGLEY_ENV` environment variable (defaulting to `dev` for local/VM runs and `prod` for scheduled GitHub Actions cloud runs).
- **Grafana Variable Dropdown:** Dashboards will feature an `Environment` template variable ($environment) allowing filtering by `prod`, `dev`, or `all`.

---

## Key Metric Categories (Grafana Dashboard Feed Candidates)

### 1. LLM & Token Consumption Telemetry
- `llm_tokens_consumed_total{environment, vendor, model, type}`: Count of prompt tokens, completion tokens, and total tokens used by extraction and review agents (Gemini 2.5 Flash, OpenAI gpt-4o-mini, Anthropic Claude).
- `llm_estimated_cost_usd_total{environment, vendor, model}`: Aggregated dollar cost estimate based on token counts.
- `llm_tier_fallback_activations_total{environment, from_tier, to_tier}`: Number of times the extraction agent fell back (e.g. Tier 1 Gemini -> Tier 3 Lexicon).

### 2. API Quota & Rate Limit Telemetry
- `api_quota_consumption_current{environment, service}`: Live quota usage counter (e.g., Finlight.me hard safety cap at 150 calls/month).
- `api_quota_remaining_ratio{environment, service}`: Percentage of available API quota remaining before automatic throttling.
- `api_http_requests_total{environment, service, status_code}`: Total HTTP requests made to external data sources (NOAA NWS, SPC convective endpoints via `wxs.us`, yfinance, arXiv).
- `api_rate_limit_throttling_total{environment, service}`: Count of HTTP 429 rate limit responses or retry loops triggered.

### 3. Pipeline Runtime & Execution Latency Telemetry
- `pipeline_execution_duration_seconds{environment, stage}`: End-to-end and stage-by-stage execution timings (Event Extraction, Feature Fusion, Quantitative Estimation, Metro Regional Calibration Agents, Web Dashboard Generation).
- `agent_task_latency_seconds{environment, agent_name}`: Execution latency per regional calibration agent (Tulsa, Newark, Cincinnati, Greenville, Charlotte, Oakland).

### 4. Operational Health & Error Telemetry
- `pipeline_errors_total{environment, module, error_type}`: Counter for uncaught exceptions, network timeouts, schema parsing failures, and data validation errors.
- `pipeline_run_status{environment, run_type}`: Binary gauge (1 = success, 0 = failure) for daily forecast runs and weekly model performance reviews.

### 5. System Compute Telemetry
- `process_cpu_seconds_total{environment}`: CPU usage during pipeline execution.
- `process_resident_memory_bytes{environment}`: RAM memory footprint during data processing on `dev-vm` vs cloud runner.

---

## Exporter & Integration Targets (Grafana Feed Options)

1. **Prometheus Endpoint (Recommended):** Expose a `GET /metrics` endpoint on `src/api_server.py` using `prometheus_client` or write static `data/telemetry.prom` for Prometheus Node Exporter textfile collector.
2. **Grafana Loki / JSON Log Stream:** Emit structured JSON telemetry lines (`logs/telemetry.log`) tagged with `"environment": "dev"` or `"prod"`, ingested by Promtail / Loki.
3. **OpenTelemetry (OTel):** Emit OTel trace spans and metric instruments to an OpenTelemetry Collector tagged with `deployment.environment`.

---

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Create central telemetry collector module (`src/telemetry.py`).
- [ ] Support `MIDGLEY_ENV` environment variable (`dev` vs `prod`) and attach `environment` label to all metrics and log entries.
- [ ] Instrument LLM token counting and vendor model breakdown across `src/event_analyzer.py`.
- [ ] Instrument API quota tracking for Finlight (`src/finlight_feed.py`), NOAA (`src/noaa_weather.py`), and market feeds.
- [ ] Record timing metrics for pipeline execution stages and sub-agents.
- [ ] Expose `/metrics` endpoint compatible with Prometheus scraping for Grafana.
- [ ] Export sample Grafana Dashboard JSON definition (`grafana/dashboard_observability.json`) with an `Environment` multi-select dropdown filter (`prod`, `dev`).

---

## Motivations & Value
- **Environment Isolation:** Enables clear side-by-side comparison of dev testing vs production automated runs without polluting production metrics.
- **Quota Safety:** Prevents unexpected API lockouts or bill shocks across free-tier and paid LLM/weather APIs.
- **Performance Optimization:** Identifies pipeline bottlenecks and latency regressions across regional agent executions.
- **Grafana Dashboard Integration:** Provides standard metrics streams for single-pane-of-glass operational monitoring.

Inland river systems are critical supply arteries for crude oil and refined petroleum products:

2. **Refinery Cooling Tower Thermal Limits:**
   - Summer river water temperatures (`00010`) above 28°C reduce cooling efficiency and trigger EPA thermal discharge compliance cutbacks, lowering refinery throughput.
3. **Estuarine Salt-Front Intrusion:**

| **World Air Quality (WAQI / AQICN)** | **Independent / International** | $\text{AQI}, \text{O}_3, \text{NO}_2, \text{SO}_2, \text{PM}_{2.5}$ | $30,000+$ global official & institutional stations | Real-time | Geo-bounding box fallback for regional metro models |
| **Sentinel-5P TROPOMI / Copernicus** | **ESA Remote Sensing** | Tropospheric $\text{SO}_2, \text{NO}_2, \text{CH}_4$ columns | Global 3.5km x 5.5km satellite grid | Daily orbital pass | Orbital verification of massive Permian/Gulf flaring plumes |

### Recommended Tri-Tiered Strategy
Midgley will implement a **tri-tiered fallback and cross-validation model**:
1. **Tier 1 (Hyper-Local Fence-Line Detection):** **PurpleAir API** for sub-minute particulate surge detection downwind of refining targets.
2. **Tier 2 (Chemical Gas Verification):** **OpenAQ API** for $\text{SO}_2$ and $\text{NO}_2$ chemical verification to rule out non-refinery smoke (e.g. agricultural burning or wildfires).
3. **Tier 3 (Regulatory Baseline & Fallback):** **EPA AirNow API** & **WAQI** for statutory Ozone Action Day tracking and fallback coverage.

---

## 2. Target Refining Hub Lat/Lon Coordinates & Fence-Line Sensor Polygons

The ingestion engine will continuously monitor 15 km radii downwind of Midgley's key refining hubs:

1. **West Tulsa, OK Hub (Tulsa Metro Calibration):**
   - **Target:** HF Sinclair West Tulsa Refinery ($125,000\text{ bpd}$)
   - **Coordinates:** $36.1384^\circ\text{ N}, 96.0125^\circ\text{ W}$ (Tulsa County, OKZ060)
   - **Monitors:** PurpleAir Tulsa sensors + EPA Site `40-143-0112`.
2. **SF Bay Area Refining Corridor (Oakland / Bay Area Calibration):**
   - **Targets:** Chevron Richmond ($245,000\text{ bpd}$), PBF Martinez ($156,000\text{ bpd}$), Valero Benicia ($145,000\text{ bpd}$)
   - **Coordinates:** $37.9542^\circ\text{ N}, 122.3853^\circ\text{ W}$ & $38.0194^\circ\text{ N}, 122.1342^\circ\text{ W}$ (Contra Costa County)
   - **Monitors:** Dense PurpleAir Bay Area fence-line sensors + BAAQMD / OpenAQ stations.
3. **Delaware City Hub (Newark Metro Calibration):**
   - **Target:** PBF Delaware City Refinery ($180,000\text{ bpd}$)
   - **Coordinates:** $39.5636^\circ\text{ N}, 75.6322^\circ\text{ W}$ (New Castle County, DE)
   - **Monitors:** PurpleAir New Castle sensors + DNREC / OpenAQ station.
4. **Catlettsburg Hub (Cincinnati Tri-State Calibration):**
   - **Target:** Marathon Catlettsburg Refinery ($291,000\text{ bpd}$)
   - **Coordinates:** $38.3972^\circ\text{ N}, 82.5978^\circ\text{ W}$ (Boyd County, KY / Tri-State)
   - **Monitors:** OpenAQ Boyd County KY + PurpleAir Ashland/Huntington sensors.

---

## 3. Mathematical & Algorithmic Design

### A. Anomaly Detection Score ($Z_{\text{AQI}}$)
For each target refining hub $h$, baseline mean $\mu_{h}$ and standard deviation $\sigma_{h}$ are calculated over a rolling 30-day window for $\text{PM}_{2.5}$ and $\text{SO}_2$:

\[
Z_{h, t} = \frac{X_{h, t} - \mu_{h, 30\text{d}}}{\sigma_{h, 30\text{d}}}
\]

* **Unplanned Outage Trigger:** If $Z_{\text{PM2.5}} > 3.5$ AND $Z_{\text{SO2}} > 2.5$ for $\ge 2$ consecutive readings, emit an **Unplanned Refinery Outage Alert**.
* **Impact Mapping:** $+\$0.15\text{ to }+\$0.35/\text{gal}$ regional rack margin surge depending on refinery capacity.

### B. Exponential Memory Fusion Integration
The resulting anomaly score vector feeds into `src/feature_engineering.py` decaying with a half-life $t_{1/2} = 4.0\text{ days}$:

\[
\text{Memory}_{\text{AQI}, t} = \text{Memory}_{\text{AQI}, t-1} \times e^{-\frac{\ln(2)}{4.0}} + \text{Shock}_{\text{AQI}, t}
\]

---

title: feat(docs/math): Leverage CodeCogs LaTeX rendering service for equation images across GitHub Markdown & web embeds
body: ### Summary & Context Currently, mathematical equations across the project—including in `AGENTS.md`, `README.md`, GitHub pull requests/issues, and the public web dashboard (`docs/math.html`)—rely on raw LaTeX text notation (`$$\dots$$`, `\(\dots\)`) or client-side JavaScript rendering via KaTeX. While KaTeX provides interactive rendering in modern web browsers, raw LaTeX syntax fails to render cleanly in many external contexts: - **GitHub Markdown previews** in mobile apps, email notifications, and third-party RSS/Markdown engines. - **Discord / Slack / Teams embeds** when sharing model documentation, decay half-lives, and forecast equations. - **Static API & MCP responses** where clients need rendered vector graphic images (SVG) or raster images (PNG) without requiring client-side JS execution. To solve this, we propose integrating the **CodeCogs LaTeX Rendering Engine** ([Documentation](https://editor.codecogs.com/docs/4-LaTeX_rendering.php)) to dynamically render high-resolution vector (SVG) and raster (PNG) equation images for documentation, static web fallbacks, and API integrations. --- ### Key Capabilities of CodeCogs LaTeX Service Per the [CodeCogs Documentation](https://editor.codecogs.com/docs/4-LaTeX_rendering.php): - **Base Endpoint Syntax:** `https://latex.codecogs.com/{type}.{format}?{LaTeX_markup}` - **Supported Output Formats (`type`):** - `svg`: Scalable Vector Graphic (crisp on high-DPI / retina displays, recommended default). - `png`: Portable Network Graphics (universal raster image support). - `gif`: Graphics Interchange Format with baseline offset header. - `json`: Returns base64-encoded image string with equation metadata (`width`, `height`, `url`, `base64`). - **Supported Receiving Modes (`format`):** - `image`: Direct image HTTP stream. - `json`: JSON object containing base64 payload. - `download`: Triggers inline browser file download. - **In-line Styling Control Parameters:** - Font scaling: `\tiny`, `\small`, `\large`, `\LARGE`, `\huge` - Dots per inch (DPI): `\dpi{150}`, `\dpi{300}` - Color styling: `\fg{#}` (foreground color hex) and `\bg{#}` (background color hex/preset) --- ### Proposed Implementation Plan #### 1. Python LaTeX URL Generator Utility (`src/utils/latex_renderer.py`) Create a dedicated utility module to parse LaTeX math strings and format clean, URL-encoded CodeCogs render endpoints: ```python def build_codecogs_url(latex: str, output_type: str = "svg", fg_color: str = "FFFFFF", bg_color: str = "transparent", dpi: int = 150) -> str: """Generates a CodeCogs LaTeX equation rendering URL.""" ... ``` #### 2. Documentation & GitHub Markdown Enhancements (`README.md` & `AGENTS.md`) Replace or supplement raw text LaTeX expressions in markdown files with SVG image tags using CodeCogs rendering, ensuring equations render natively across all GitHub platforms, mobile apps, and external Markdown viewports: ```html ``` #### 3. Public Web Dashboard Export & Fallback (`src/dashboard_generator.py` & `docs/math.html`) - Add a "Copy CodeCogs Image Tag" / "Download Equation SVG" feature to each math section in `docs/math.html`. - Provide an inline SVG image fallback for environments where CDN JavaScript execution (KaTeX) is disabled or blocked. #### 4. REST API & MCP Server Integration (`src/api_server.py` & `src/mcp_server.py`) - Expose a new REST API endpoint `GET /api/v1/math/render` that accepts a LaTeX formula string and returns the formatted CodeCogs SVG/PNG URL along with optional base64 JSON payload. - Expose an MCP tool `get_equation_image` enabling LLMs and AI agents to fetch equation image links for rich UI presentation. --- ### Acceptance Criteria - [ ] Implement `src/utils/latex_renderer.py` helper function with URL encoding, styling parameters (`\fg`, `\bg`, `\dpi`), and unit test suite. - [ ] Embed CodeCogs SVG equations into `README.md` and `AGENTS.md` for core model equations (Memory Fusion, Ridge Regression, Regional Metro Rack Margins). - [ ] Update `src/dashboard_generator.py` to add CodeCogs SVG export links and static fallbacks to `docs/math.html`. - [ ] Add REST API `/api/v1/math/render` and MCP tool `get_equation_image` for external client integration. - [ ] Validate image rendering across dark and light GitHub themes.

### 🚚 Feature Proposal: Ultra-Low Sulfur Diesel (ULSD) Forecasting & Distillate Crack Spread Modeling

#### 🛢️ Overview & Feature Vision
Expand `midgley` beyond Unleaded RBOB Gasoline (`RB=F`) by introducing a full quantitative forecasting engine, physical feature pipeline, regional calibration agent, and scenario simulator for **Ultra-Low Sulfur Diesel (ULSD)** (`HO=F` NY Harbor ULSD futures).

Diesel fuel powers global commercial logistics, long-haul trucking fleets, agricultural harvesting, freight rail, maritime shipping, and emergency industrial generation. Modeling diesel brings a crucial economic and physical energy dimension to the `midgley` multi-agent framework!

#### 💡 Problem & Value Proposition
Gasoline (`RB=F`) and Diesel (`HO=F`) exhibit distinct fundamental supply-demand dynamics and seasonal cycles:
- **Seasonal Divergence**: Gasoline demand peaks during the summer driving season (May–September), while diesel demand peaks during the autumn agricultural harvest (Sept–Nov) and winter heating/freight season (Nov–March due to residential heating oil pool overlap).
- **Cracking Dynamics**: Unleaded gas is driven by the RBOB-WTI crack spread, whereas diesel is governed by the **ULSD Distillate Crack Spread** ($\text{HO=F} - \text{CL=F}/42$) and 3-2-1 refinery yield economics.
- **Regulatory Overhead**: Federal diesel excise tax ($0.244/gal) exceeds federal gasoline tax ($0.184/gal), while state-level renewable fuel mandates (D4 Biomass-Based Diesel RINs and CARB Renewable Diesel / RD99 standards) introduce unique price spread behaviors.

Adding diesel forecasting allows fleet operators, trucking managers, agricultural producers, and energy analysts to anticipate 5-day ULSD wholesale and retail price trajectories and optimize fuel procurement strategies.

#### 🛠️ Key Technical & Architectural Modules

1. **Distillate Market Data Ingestion (`src/data_ingestion.py` & `src/live_fuel_feed.py`)**:
   - Ingest NYMEX Ultra-Low Sulfur Diesel / Heating Oil futures (`HO=F`).
   - Fetch EIA Weekly Distillate Fuel Oil Inventories, PADD-level stocks, and refinery distillate production rates.
   - Track USGC, NY Harbor, and Los Angeles ULSD spot prices.

2. **Distillate Crack Spread & Physical Feature Engineering (`src/feature_engineering.py`)**:
   - **3-2-1 Crack Spread**:

3. **Quantitative ULSD Forecasting Engine (`src/models.py`)**:
   - Fit regularized Ridge ($\alpha=10.0$) and XGBoost regressors tailored to ULSD time series.
   - Generate 5-day out-of-time ULSD wholesale commodity forecasts ($/gal).

4. **Regional Diesel Metro Calibration Agents (`src/diesel_regional.py`)**:

   - **West Coast / Oakland Metro**: Calibrated to CARB ULSD specifications, LCFS carbon credit overhead, D4 RIN pricing, and Renewable Diesel (RD99/B20) blending dynamics.

5. **Counterfactual Diesel Physical & Geopolitical Shock Simulator (`main.py` / `src/diesel_shocks.py`)**:

## Feature Request: Oakland, CA Metro Area Expansion (PADD 5 West Coast) & CARB Regulatory Cost Display

### Summary
Expand Midgley's regional forecasting capabilities by adding **Oakland, CA & the San Francisco Bay Area (PADD 5 West Coast)** as a dedicated regional model and public dashboard locale. With a baseline pump price anchor of **~$4.950/gal** (compared to $3.890 in Tulsa, $3.350 in Newark, and $3.450 in Cincinnati), Oakland represents the highest-cost, most highly-regulated regional market in the nation, providing a stark baseline comparison ("scare factor") for users across all other metropolitan areas.

### Regional Infrastructure, PADD 5 Isolation & Regulatory Cost Drivers
1. **Unprecedented Tax & Environmental Regulatory Burden**:
   - **California Excise Tax**: 63.4¢/gal (adjusted July 1, 2026).
   - **Cap-and-Trade (Cap-and-Invest) Program**: ~25.0¢/gal carbon allowance cost.
   - **Low Carbon Fuel Standard (LCFS)**: ~18.5¢/gal compliance credit deficit cost.
   - **State/Local Sales Taxes & Underground Storage Tank Fee**: ~15.0¢/gal.
   - **Federal Excise Tax**: 18.4¢/gal.
   - **Total Regulatory & Tax Burden**: **~95.3¢/gal** embedded into every gallon at Oakland pumps (vs $0.190 in OK or $0.385 in OH).
2. **PADD 5 "Refining Island" Geographic Isolation**:
   - Zero interstate refined product pipelines cross the Rocky Mountains or Sierra Nevada into California.
   - San Francisco Bay Area refined product deficits cannot be backfilled from Gulf Coast (PADD 3) or Midwest (PADD 2) pipeline infrastructure; shortfalls must be imported via ocean oil tankers from Asia/Middle East (3+ week transit) or Alaska North Slope (ANS) crude maritime routes.
3. **SF Bay Area Refining Hub & Local Infrastructure**:
   - **Chevron Richmond Refinery** (Contra Costa County, 245,000 bpd capacity): Directly adjacent to Oakland; primary regional producer of CARB Reformulated Gasoline (CaRFG).
   - **PBF Energy Martinez Refinery** (156,000 bpd capacity) & **Valero Benicia Refinery** (145,000 bpd capacity).
   - **Marathon Martinez Facility**: Converted to renewable diesel, contracting total regional crude refining capacity.
4. **Distribution Logistics**:
   - **Kinder Morgan SFPP (Santa Fe Pacific Pipeline) System**: Originates at Richmond/Concord terminals, distributing fuel across Northern California and Nevada (Reno/Sparks).
5. **CARB Reformulated Gasoline (CaRFG) Transition**:
   - Seasonal transition to CaRFG summer blend (effective April 1) adds +15¢–25¢/gal refining premium and surges volatility during spring refinery maintenance turnarounds.
6. **Localized Weather & Infrastructure Shocks**:
   - Atmospheric river winter storms & refinery grid disruptions (PG&E PSPS power outages).
   - NOAA Alerts for Alameda County (CAZ508) and Contra Costa County (CAZ511).

### Implementation Plan
- [ ] `src/oakland_regional.py`: Oakland market data ingestion ($4.950/gal anchor), Richmond refinery crack spread calculation, CARB regulatory cost layer, SF Bay regional events, and NOAA CAZ508 weather dataset.
- [ ] `oakland_main.py`: Standalone 6-step regional forecasting pipeline with Oakland shock scenario simulations (Chevron Richmond flaring outage, CaRFG summer blend switch, atmospheric river grid failure).
- [ ] `build_oakland_notebook.py` & `notebooks/oakland_gas_price_llm_forecasting.ipynb`: Programmatic notebook generator and interactive Jupyter notebook.

title: feat(lubelogger): LubeLogger integration for predictive vehicle tank refill & fuel cost optimization
body:
### Feature Proposal: LubeLogger Integration for Predictive Tank Refill & Fuel Cost Optimization

#### 🛢️ Overview
Integrate `midgley` with **[LubeLogger](https://github.com/hargata/lubelog)** (the self-hosted vehicle management platform) to predict precisely **when and how much** gas a user should put in their vehicle to minimize total fuel expenditure.

#### 💡 Problem & Value Proposition
Standard fuel tracking tools only look backwards (recording historical fill-up costs and MPG). Meanwhile, gas price forecasts only look forward at market prices. 

By combining **LubeLogger's vehicle telemetry** (tank capacity, current estimated fuel level, average MPG, and daily driving rate) with **`midgley`'s 5-day regional price forecasts**, the system can answer the ultimate driver question: 
> *"Given my current tank level and daily commute, should I fill up today, wait a few days for a price dip, or put in a temporary splash of gas to bridge until prices drop?"*

#### 🛠️ Key Integration Capabilities

1. **LubeLogger API Sync (`src/lubelogger_client.py`)**:
   - Connects to LubeLogger's REST API (`/api/vehicle/fuellogs`, `/api/vehicle`) to pull vehicle specs, last odometer reading, fuel log history, average consumption (MPG or L/100km), and tank capacity.
   - Estimates current tank fuel level (%) and remaining range based on days/miles elapsed since last logged fill-up.

2. **Cost-Optimal Tank Refill Algorithm (`src/refill_optimizer.py`)**:
   - Evaluates vehicle range decay against `midgley`'s 5-day regional metro price trajectory ($/gal).
   - Generates actionable refill strategies:
     - 🚀 **Early Fill Recommendation**: Tank is at ~45%, but local gas prices are forecasted to jump +$0.15/gal in 48 hours (e.g., weekend gap or supply shock). ➔ *Recommendation: Fill up full tank today before price hike.*
     - ⏳ **Deferred Fill Recommendation**: Tank is low (~20%), but prices are projected to drop -$0.20/gal over the next 4 days. ➔ *Recommendation: Put \$10 (2-3 gal) in today to bridge commute, then full fill-up on Tuesday at lowest projected price.*
     - 🟢 **Standard Fill Window**: Prices stable; fill up as normal when tank reaches reserve threshold.

3. **Notification & Automation Triggers**:
   - Webhook & Push Notifications (Telegram, Apprise, Home Assistant, or Email) when an optimal fill-up window opens.
   - Optional LubeLogger dashboard widget / sidecar service integration.

#### 🏗️ Architecture & Data Flow

```
[ LubeLogger REST API ] 
  (Fuel Logs, Odometer, Tank Capacity, MPG)
          │
          ▼
[ midgley Refill Optimizer ] ◄───── [ midgley 5-Day Metro Forecast Engine ]
          │
          ▼
[ Predictive Refill Action & Cost Optimization Alert ]
  • Recommended Fill Date & Target Price
  • Projected $ Savings vs Immediate Full Fill
```

#### 📋 Tasks to Complete
- [ ] Implement LubeLogger API client wrapper (`src/lubelogger_client.py`).
- [ ] Develop vehicle consumption & range decay estimator (`src/vehicle_telemetry.py`).
- [ ] Build cost-optimal refill strategy calculator (`src/refill_optimizer.py`).
- [ ] Add CLI command and configuration section in `config.yaml` / `.env` for LubeLogger API keys and vehicle IDs.
- [ ] Create Home Assistant & webhook notification integration for LubeLogger refill alerts.
